rated_messages.input_message: If you miss doing something with your hands, try turning a coin or pen over and over with your fingers.
Try to avoid seeing other people smoke. It might sound basic but brain see, brain want! If you can, make life easier and avoid the people you used to smoke with for some time where possible.

Imagine your urge is like a talk radio station going on about something you disagree with. Arguing with it doesn't change what they say. Instead, just let them talk while you focus on what's important to you.
It can be tricky to be around friends or colleagues who are still smoking. If you're finding it tough, try and think about the things that you are doing well.
What inspires you most to quit smoking? Are you willing to let this urge pass without smoking for that reason?
If leaving social situations to avoid smokers feels awkward, make sure you have something to do instead - take sugar free mints, lollipops or low fat snacks to chew, or use a stress ball.
If you are tempted to smoke by being in this location, see if you can sit with that temptation for 1 minute. When the minute is over, do it again. Soon, it should pass.
Don't test yourself needlessly. If this social situation gets uncomfortable then leave briefly if you can. It really helps and it's fine to do it more than once!

Remind yourself that by staying quit, you'll be freeing yourself from the constant cycle of cigarette, nicotine withdrawal, feeling stressed as a result and wanting another cigarette. Keep going and this will be a thing of the past!
Each time you let an urge pass without smoking, you break the old habit a bit more.
